summary.text: Roy Caldwell is the Republican candidate for the Montana House of Representatives, District 84, in the November 3, 2026 general election. A retired U.S. Air Force officer and Academy graduate, he won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary over James Marshal and faces Democrat Tia Nelson.

paragraphs.text: Roy Caldwell served in the U.S. Air Force from 1981 to 2013 and earned a bachelor's degree from the United States Air Force Academy in 1985, according to Ballotpedia.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he later earned a master's degree in Space Systems Management from Webster University and that his Air Force assignments included GPS satellite controller, KC-135R navigator, ROTC assistant professor, strategic planner, and project and software manager.

Caldwell said in the survey that he worked for 12 years in the private sector as an FAA-certified aircraft dispatcher, taught middle school science, and worked nearly a decade for the Department of Veterans Affairs, most recently at the Montana VA Healthcare System at Fort Harrison as a management and program/data analyst.

He said he served as a House Sergeant at Arms staffer during the 2025 legislative session, volunteers with the Boy Scouts of America and Civil Air Patrol, and serves as vice commander of American Legion Post 2 in Helena.
Caldwell defeated James Marshal in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary, 62.0 percent to 38.0 percent.

In the survey, he listed affordability, education options for parents, and limiting government overreach as his key campaign messages, and said he would seek government incentives for first-time home buyers and work to cut property taxes while watching government spending.
